daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka is expected to formally submit his resignation letter to the MPR at 11:00 WIB today, according to Komisi III DPR chair, with MPR leadership on standby to receive him. Presidential spokesperson Budi Arie confirmed Gibran's resignation as vice president, following the submission of a parliamentary impeachment motion by 120 DPR members over alleged educational credential irregularities. Gibran met President Prabowo at the palace Wednesday evening ahead of his departure, with observers noting the resignation follows weeks of political pressure.

  • National Police Chief Suyudi briefed Komisi III DPR on the five-stage operational method used in the illegal wiretapping of President Prabowo, revealing that targets extended beyond Prabowo to include KPK officials, governors, and activists.
  • Komisi III DPR asserted that the wiretapping case involving Listyo Sigit falls under the category of treason (makar), while a senior lawmaker called for a formal treason investigation.
  • National Police Chief Kapolri disclosed that former police chief Listyo Sigit also wiretapped internal National Police communications, with wiretapping orders allegedly transmitted both orally and via WhatsApp.
  • President Prabowo joked about being wiretapped during NasDem Party's anniversary celebration, while the Indonesian Muslim Intellectuals Association urged authorities to investigate the wiretapping case without favoritism.
  • National Police Chief Kapolri stated that 28 witnesses have been examined in the presidential wiretapping case, while DPR member Sahroni requested the police chief display the wiretapping equipment used by Listyo Sigit and associates.
  • National Police Chief visited Yogyakarta following recent protests, with the regional police chief noting security vulnerabilities in the area, while 21 minors arrested during violent demonstrations were returned to their families.
  • The KPK examined a former Central Java BPK head regarding alleged audit manipulation in Pemalang regency, while three former Customs officials faced sentencing hearings for import corruption.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo is confirmed to personally attend the APEC Summit in Shenzhen, China, where Indonesia will advance national resilience and AI security agendas. During the summit, President Prabowo is scheduled to meet with President Xi Jinping to discuss exploration of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) between Indonesia and China.

  • Indonesia's Foreign Ministry confirmed that an Indonesian citizen joined the Russian military and has been captured by Ukrainian forces, while police uncovered a Russian-Ukrainian syndicate recruiting mercenaries in Indonesia.
  • Indonesia and ICAO are jointly training aviation safety inspectors from eight countries in a regional capacity-building initiative.
  • Bali and Thailand are exploring enhanced cooperation in tourism and healthcare sectors during bilateral discussions.

Other

The rupiah weakened slightly to Rp18,233 per US dollar, pressured by the US Federal Reserve's interest rate increase and MSCI's announcement. The Agriculture Minister assured that rice stock remains safe at 4.5 million tons for the year-end period. The government set the October ICP at US$117.24 per barrel, with November prices projected to moderate.

  • Central Java is adding 12 new industrial zones with permits to be issued soon, while industrial parks are targeting chip technology cooperation worth Rp900 billion.
  • The government assured sufficient electricity and water supply in Batam for data center industries, while the Jakarta MRT Phase 2A tunnel work was completed at Mangga Besar station.
  • Indonesian food products recorded US$25.38 million in potential deals at the Shanghai trade exhibition, while Garuda Indonesia's MRO unit targets expansion to five countries.
  • Indonesia's drug regulator BPOM revealed a list of 11 dangerous cosmetics containing hazardous ingredients, while Aceh established emergency disaster status until January 2027 with 24-hour area monitoring.
  • Danareksa Investments targets up to Rp200 trillion in assets by 2027, while the Culture Ministry reported that Indonesia has developed 9,264 arts and culture talents.
